item.content:encoded:
Yes, great catch and thank you for double checking that! Will fix it right away. I had dug into the articles on giant tube worms and their close annelid relatives for my terminology, but hadn't looked up chemotropism specifically.

When I was in school they were still calling single celled organisms that can metabolize hydrogen sulfide "archaebacteria" which threw me for a loop at first. So when I say "achieving bacterial chemosynthesis" in the footnote it's not the most precise description scientifically. I figured it was close enough to get readers started if they wanted to look up the science parts, while still being immediately understandable. The Wikipedia articles on these animals did not provide much in the way of detail I could use for a restaurant menu, but I doubt they've been described as if they were food very often before. :3

Adult tube worms anchor themselves near sulfurous vents, opening their bodies to infection by chemotropic single-celled archaea.

Do you mean "chemotrophic" here?

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemotropism

Chemotropism is growth of organisms such as bacteria and plants, navigated by chemical stimulus from outside of the organism or organism's part.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemotroph

Chemotrophs are organisms that obtain energy by the oxidation of electron donors in their environments.

item.content:encoded:
Special thanks to Proasek for inventing the Ambrose franchise, without which this horrible idea would never have evolved! Be sure to check out Proasek's author page for more ambrosial goodness.

Big big thanks to stormbreath for a) creating Ambrose London Prix Fixe from which most of my CSS is stolen, b) helping me make the stolen code actually work, and c) giving me good crits on the text. Thanks to Uncle Nicolini for further help with CSS shenanigans. Thanks to psul on the forums and Captain Kirby in chat for giving me excellent guidance and critiques on the text.

In the mainline canon, falling under the sway of a Neo-Sarkic practitioner is close to a worst case scenario.
In End of Death it's significantly better than the default.

An up-and-coming Neo-Sarkic empire trying to entice potential noble immigrants and extradimensional tourists would need a fancy restaurant — one which lived up to the demanding and unusual tastes of their clientele. And Ambrose would be up to the challenge.
